claims.head: A shadow job for Bertuzzi, Frondell and Greenway
claims.call: The Blackhawks’ L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Greenway) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ first line, against about 33% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Bertuzzi’s line (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Greenway) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Panarin, Laferriere and Kempe.

claims.gist: At home, Jeff Blashill likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ first line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 44%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

CHI.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Chicago has home-ice advantage. The Blackhawks can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.

items.text: Patrick Kane is two assists from 900.

The Kings are newly without Mats Zuccarello, have been without Alex Turcotte since Oct 6, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Capitals and the Penguins are missing more right now.
The Blackhawks have been without Bowen Byram since Oct 13.
The Blackhawks have changed their lines: NHL.com projects Ryan Greene with Roman Kantserov and Connor Bedard.
